journey.title: From idea to launch, on a production line.
journey.description: Every build moves through the same ten stages. You can see exactly which one yours is on at any moment.

idea.name: Idea
idea.detail: Describe what you want in your own words. Upload anything you already have.

configure.name: Configure
configure.detail: Pick the build type, features and design direction, or ask us to design it for you.

price.name: Price
price.detail: Your scope resolves to a fixed price and a delivery window before you commit.

pay.name: Pay
pay.detail: Checkout in your own currency. The scope you agreed is attached to the order.

build.name: Build
build.detail: The countdown starts once your assets are in and the build is officially started.

preview.name: Preview
preview.detail: Watch it come together on a live preview URL, updated as we go.

approve.name: Approve
approve.detail: Request changes within scope, then sign off when it's right.

launch.name: Launch
launch.detail: We deploy to your domain, or submit to the app stores on your behalf.

maintain.name: Maintain
maintain.detail: Hosting, updates and monitoring on a plan you can cancel.

expand.name: Expand
expand.detail: Add features later with build credits, at the same published rates.

journey.clockNote: The guaranteed countdown starts at this stage, once your assets are in.

guarantee.title: The deadline is ours to keep.

clock.title: Your clock starts when the work can start
clock.body: The countdown begins when your required information and assets are submitted and the build is officially started, not the moment you pay. We don't start a clock we can't control.

missed.title: If we miss it, you choose
missed.continue: Continue the build and take {percent}% back.
missed.body: Either way the choice is yours, not ours, and it doesn't require a negotiation.

stores.title: What the guarantee doesn't cover
stores.body: App Store and Google Play review times sit outside the development guarantee. We commit to our build time; we can't commit to theirs. You'll see submission and review tracked separately in your Build Room.

scope.title: A fixed price needs an honest scope.
scope.description: A {days}-Day Build covers a defined set of capabilities. When an idea needs more than that, we say so before you pay and show you the larger build, rather than underquoting and renegotiating later.

includedItems.pages: A defined page or screen count
includedItems.forms: Forms, content pages and standard CMS editing
includedItems.singleRole: A single user type, or none at all

largerItems.multiRole: Several user types with different permissions
largerItems.realtime: Live tracking, dispatch or location features
largerItems.marketplace: Multi-party payouts or a marketplace model
largerItems.integrations: Custom integrations with systems you already run
largerItems.logic: Operational logic that has to be designed, not configured

example.title: A worked example
example.quote: I want a restaurant system where customers order food, pay online, restaurant staff manage orders, drivers manage deliveries, and customers track drivers.
example.reason: It carries four distinct user types, live driver tracking, delivery dispatch and payment handling. Each of those is real work, so it resolves to a larger build with its own price and timeline, which you'll see before you pay.
example.note: Nothing here is guesswork: the configurator applies the same published rules to your description and shows you which ones it matched.

buildWall.title: Recently shipped
buildWall.description: Every build that goes live, with the scope it was ordered under and the days it took.
buildWall.emptyTitle: The first builds are in production
buildWall.emptyBody: Completed builds appear here with their scope and delivery time once they launch. Nothing is staged or illustrative, so the wall stays empty until there is something real to show.

cta.title: Start with the idea. We'll price it in minutes.
cta.description: Describe what you want and see your scope, price and delivery date before you commit to anything.

configuratorEntry.title: Four steps to a fixed price.
configuratorEntry.description: Nothing is charged until you have seen the scope, the price and the delivery date. Most people get through this in under ten minutes.

describe.label: Describe
describe.detail: What you want, in plain words

configuratorEntry.reassurance: No account needed to see your price.

comparison.title: Website, system, or app.
comparison.description: The difference is not size, it is what the thing has to do. Pick the row that describes your problem.
comparison.footnote: Anything beyond these rows is still buildable; it simply resolves to a larger build with its own price and timeline, which you will see before you pay.

design.title: You do not need a designer to start.
design.description: Most people ordering a first website have a logo at best. All three routes below cost the same; they only change how much you hand over.

design_for_me.title: Design it for me
design_for_me.body: Tell us the business and the feeling you want. We choose the typography, colour and layout, and show you the result in the preview.
design_for_me.note: Most common for a first build.

supplied_brand.title: I have brand assets
supplied_brand.body: Upload your logo, colours, fonts or a brand guide. We build to them rather than inventing a new look alongside your existing one.

existing_design.title: Rebuild what I have
existing_design.body: Point us at an existing site, a Figma file or screenshots. We rebuild it properly rather than starting the conversation again.
existing_design.note: A link or a screenshot is enough.

design.footnote: Whichever route you choose, you own the result outright: the design, the code and the content are yours, with no licence to keep paying for.

maintenance.title: Keeping it running is a separate decision.
maintenance.description: The build is bought once. Hosting, updates and monitoring are a monthly plan you can cancel, because folding them into the headline price would make that price untrue from month two.
maintenance.footnote: You can also host it yourself. We hand over the code and the deployment either way, and no plan is required to keep your build.

essential.name: Essential
essential.summary: Keep it online and backed up.

priority.summary: For builds the business depends on.

features.priorityQueue: Priority place in the build queue

faq.title: The things worth asking first.
faq.description: If something here is unclear, that is our problem to fix, not yours to decode.

included.q: What exactly do I get for the price?
included.a: A finished, deployed build matching the scope you agreed, plus the code and design files. The scope is written down before you pay and is what the price is attached to — that is the whole point of a fixed price.

ownership.q: Do I own what you build?
ownership.a: Yes, entirely. The code, the design and the content are yours on delivery, with no ongoing licence and nothing held back. You can move it to another host or another developer whenever you want, and we will hand over everything needed to do that.

clockStart.q: When does the countdown actually start?
clockStart.a: When your required information and assets are in and the build is officially started — not when you pay. We do not start a clock we cannot control, and you will see the exact start time in your Build Room.

missedDeadline.q: What happens if you miss the deadline?
missedDeadline.a: You choose, not us. Either cancel and take a 100% refund, or let the build continue and take 30% back. It does not require a negotiation and there is no process to argue your way through.

biggerIdea.q: What if my idea is bigger than a 5-Day Build?
biggerIdea.a: The configurator tells you before you pay, and shows which specific capabilities pushed it over — multiple user types, live tracking, multi-party payouts and so on. It then offers the larger build with its own price and timeline, rather than underquoting and renegotiating later.

changes.q: How many changes can I ask for?
changes.a: Changes within the agreed scope are expected and do not affect your delivery date. Changes that add capability are priced as additions, and you will see the figure before anything is built.

hosting.q: Do I have to buy a maintenance plan?
hosting.a: No. You can host it yourself and never pay us again. The plans exist because most people would rather not think about SSL certificates and backups, not because your build stops working without one.

appStores.q: Does the 14 days include App Store approval?
appStores.a: No, and we are explicit about that. We guarantee our development time. Apple and Google control their own review queues and we cannot promise someone else's timeline. Submission and review are tracked separately in your Build Room.

refund.q: How does the refund actually work?
refund.a: It returns to the original payment method, through Stripe, and we start it the same day you choose it. There is no form to fill in and no retention conversation.

different.q: How is this different from hiring an agency?
different.a: An agency sells you a relationship priced by the hour, where the scope and the date move together. This is a product with a published price, a defined scope and a date that costs us money if we miss it. If your project genuinely needs an open-ended engagement, an agency is the right answer and we will say so.
